The bill would create an independent Social Security Commission to advise Parliament on minimum social security payment levels.
The Commission would review payments under the Social Security Act 1991 and recommend increases or changes to indexation if current levels do not meet an acceptable standard of living.
The Commission must ensure recipients do not fall below the poverty line, using international definitions, and the Minister must table reviews and respond to recommendations.
Requires the Commission to conduct reviews of social security payment adequacy.
Requires the Minister to table Commission reviews and provide a detailed response.
Recipients of social security payments under the Social Security Act 1991.

The speaker argued that social security payments are falling behind the cost of living and supported the Social Security Commission Bill 2018, which would establish an independent commission to review and publicly report on all payment rates.
